s:
Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (Launch vehicle):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Launch vehicle)
a. DS-SAR | i. PSLV-C56
b. Aditya-L1 | ii. GSLV-F15
c. RISAT-2BR1 | iii. PSLV-C48
d. NVS-02 | iv. PSLV-C57
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: DS-SAR (Singapore radar satellite) – PSLV-C56, July 2023; Aditya-L1 – PSLV-C57, Sep 2023; RISAT-2BR1 – PSLV-C48, Dec 2019; NVS-02 (NavIC) – GSLV-F15, Jan 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about recent ISRO launches:
1. RISAT-1, launched by PSLV-C19 in 2012, carries an X-band Synthetic Aperture Radar.
2. EOS-07 was launched by SSLV-D2 on 10 February 2023.
3. EOS-08, launched by SSLV-D3 in August 2024, was the last development flight of the SSLV.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: RISAT-1 (PSLV-C19, 2012) carries a C-band SAR for day-night, all-weather imaging; X-band radar is on RISAT-2BR1.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. INSAT-3DS, a meteorological satellite launched by GSLV-F14, was funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
2. NVS-02, a NavIC satellite launched by GSLV-F15 in January 2025, missed its intended orbit.
3. NISAR, the Earth observation mission with NASA, was launched by GSLV-F17 in July 2025.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: NISAR flew on GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025; GSLV-F17 launched EOS-05 (4 Sep 2026).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The SpaDeX mission is a key step towards the Bharatiya Antariksh Station.
Reason (R): Building and servicing a space station needs docking, which SpaDeX demonstrated when its two spacecraft docked on 16 January 2025.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: docking capability is needed for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (and Chandrayaan-4); SpaDeX (PSLV-C60) docked on 16 Jan 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about records of Indian launch vehicles:
1. BlueBird Block-2 (about 6,100 kg), a direct-to-smartphone broadband satellite launched by LVM3-M6, is the heaviest payload launched by an Indian rocket.
2. The first dedicated commercial flight of the LVM3 carried 36 OneWeb satellites in 2022.
3. Kalpana-1, India's first exclusive weather satellite, was launched by the GSLV in 2002.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Kalpana-1 (2002) was launched by the PSLV.

s:
Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (Builder):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Builder)
a. ANUSAT | i. IIT Kanpur
b. Jugnu | ii. NMIT Bengaluru
c. STUDSAT-2 | iii. Anna University
d. WeSAT | iv. LBS Institute of Technology for Women
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ANUSAT (2009) – Anna University, the first student satellite launched by ISRO; Jugnu (PSLV-C18, 2011) – IIT Kanpur; STUDSAT-2 – NMIT Bengaluru; WeSAT (on POEM-3) – LBS Institute of Technology for Women.

s:
Match List-I (Satellite launched by ISRO) with List-II (Country / agency):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Country / agency)
a. KITSAT-3 | i. Italy
b. AGILE | ii. European Space Agency
c. NovaSAR | iii. South Korea
d. Proba-3 | iv. United Kingdom
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: KITSAT-3 – South Korea (PSLV-C2, 1999); AGILE – Italy, gamma-ray astronomy (PSLV-C8, 2007); NovaSAR – UK (PSLV-C42, 2018); Proba-3 – ESA (PSLV-C59, Dec 2024).

s:
Consider the following statements about ISRO's foreign customer launches:
1. ISRO has launched 433 foreign satellites of more than 34 countries.
2. More than half of these foreign satellites belong to the United Kingdom.
3. ISRO launched 72 OneWeb satellites in two LVM3 missions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: over half of the 433 foreign satellites are from the United States; OneWeb (UK) supplied the 72 satellites flown on two LVM3 missions.

s:
Consider the following statements about private Indian satellites:
1. TSAT-1A, a sub-metre optical satellite, was built by Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic at Vemagal in Karnataka.
2. Pixxel's hyperspectral satellite Shakuntala (TD-2) was India's first private commercial imaging satellite.
3. Both TSAT-1A and Shakuntala were launched by ISRO's PSLV.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: both TSAT-1A (Apr 2024) and Shakuntala (Apr 2022) were launched on SpaceX's Falcon 9.

s:
Match List-I (Failed mission) with List-II (Payload lost):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Payload lost)
a. GSLV-F02 (2006) | i. EOS-02 and AzaadiSAT
b. GSLV-F10 (2021) | ii. EOS-09
c. SSLV-D1 (2022) | iii. EOS-03
d. PSLV-C61 (2025) | iv. INSAT-4C
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: GSLV-F02 lost INSAT-4C; GSLV-F10 lost EOS-03 (cryogenic stage); SSLV-D1 put EOS-02 and AzaadiSAT in a wrong orbit; PSLV-C61 (18 May 2025) lost EOS-09 (third stage).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The PSLV-C62 mission of 12 January 2026 failed because its first stage did not ignite.
Reason (R): PSLV-C62 lost EOS-N1 'Anvesha' along with 15 co-passenger satellites.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: the failure was a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage, not first-stage non-ignition. R is true: EOS-N1 'Anvesha' and 15 co-passengers were lost.

s:
Match List-I (Experiment) with List-II (Launch vehicle, year):
List-I (Experiment) | List-II (Vehicle, year)
a. SRE-1 (Space Capsule Recovery Experiment) | i. PSLV-C58, 2024
b. CARE (crew module re-entry) | ii. PSLV-C53, 2022
c. POEM | iii. PSLV-C7, 2007
d. POEM-3 | iv. LVM3, 2014
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: SRE-1 – PSLV-C7 (2007); CARE – LVM3 (2014); POEM – PSLV-C53 (2022); POEM-3 – PSLV-C58 (2024) (POEM-2 was on C55, 2023).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM) uses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital laboratory.
2. TRISHNA, a thermal infrared mission to measure land surface temperature and water stress, is a joint mission of ISRO and JAXA.
3. Proba-3 uses formation flying of two spacecraft to create an artificial solar eclipse for studying the corona.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: ISRO's partner in TRISHNA is CNES (France), not JAXA.

s:
Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (Application):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Application)
a. EMISAT | i. Ocean studies
b. Oceansat | ii. Electronic intelligence
c. NVS series | iii. Science (X-ray polarimetry)
d. XPoSat | iv. Navigation (NavIC)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: EMISAT – electronic intelligence (strategic); Oceansat – ocean; NVS – NavIC navigation; XPoSat – science, with Aditya-L1.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The James Webb Space Telescope, launched on 25 December 2021, is a joint mission of NASA, ESA and CSA.
2. The James Webb Space Telescope observes mainly in the X-ray part of the spectrum.
3. With XPoSat, India became the second country, after NASA's IXPE, to launch a dedicated X-ray polarimetry satellite.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: JWST is an infrared telescope; X-ray polarimetry is the field of IXPE (NASA, Dec 2021) and XPoSat.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mars missions:
1. NASA's Perseverance rover landed in the Jezero crater in February 2021 along with the Ingenuity helicopter.
2. The rover of ESA's ExoMars mission is named Rosalind Franklin.
3. Beagle-2, the lander carried on ESA's Mars Express in 2003, was built by France.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Beagle-2 was a British-built lander; it was lost on landing and found on the surface in 2015.

s:
Match List-I (Space mission / rocket) with List-II (Country):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Country)
a. SuperView | i. South Korea
b. Nuri (KSLV-II) | ii. Japan
c. EQUULEUS | iii. Israel and France
d. VENµS | iv. China
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: SuperView – China (commercial Earth observation); Nuri – South Korea's first indigenous launcher (June 2022); EQUULEUS – JAXA's steam-propelled CubeSat; VENµS – Israel-France vegetation and environment satellite (2017).

s:
Match List-I (Chinese lunar mission) with List-II (Achievement):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Achievement)
a. Chang'e-3 (2013) | i. First soil brought back from the far side of the Moon
b. Chang'e-4 (2019) | ii. China's first lunar sample return
c. Chang'e-5 (2020) | iii. First soft landing on the far side of the Moon
d. Chang'e-6 (2024) | iv. China's first soft landing on the Moon
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Chang'e-3 – China's first soft landing (first by anyone since 1976); Chang'e-4 – first far-side soft landing (rover Yutu-2); Chang'e-5 – first Chinese sample return; Chang'e-6 – first far-side soil (returned 25 Jun 2024).

s:
Consider the following statements about lunar missions:
1. NASA's LCROSS hit a polar crater of the Moon in 2009 to look for water.
2. The lunar module of Apollo 11 that landed on 20 July 1969 was named Columbia.
3. Japan's SLIM made Japan the fifth country to soft-land on the Moon.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Apollo 11 lunar module was Eagle (Columbia was the command module, not in the notes as the lander).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): India signed the US-led Artemis Accords in 2023.
Reason (R): Under NASA's Artemis programme, Artemis IV (2028) is planned as the first crewed landing, near the lunar south pole.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true (India signed in 2023; Artemis IV is now the first crewed landing after Artemis III became a 2027 low-Earth-orbit test), but the mission plan does not explain why India signed the Accords.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-3:
1. It consisted of a Propulsion Module, the lander Vikram and the rover Pragyan, with no orbiter of its own.
2. Its mission life was one lunar day, about 14 Earth days.
3. Its rover Pragyan weighed about 260 kg.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Pragyan weighed about 26 kg (the lander 1,752 kg including the rover; whole craft 3,900 kg).

s:
Consider the following statements about the landing of Chandrayaan-3:
1. Before India, only the USA, the USSR/Russia and Japan had soft-landed on the Moon.
2. The Vikram lander touched down at Shiv Shakti Point on 23 August 2023.
3. India observes 23 August as National Space Day.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the three earlier soft-landers were the USA, USSR/Russia and China; Japan's SLIM became the fifth after India.

s:
Match List-I (Chandrayaan-3 payload) with List-II (Function):
List-I (Payload) | List-II (Function)
a. ChaSTE | i. Moonquakes (seismic activity)
b. ILSA | ii. Studying the Earth from lunar orbit
c. RAMBHA-LP | iii. Plasma density
d. SHAPE | iv. Surface thermal profile
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ChaSTE (lander) – thermal profile; ILSA (lander) – moonquakes; RAMBHA-LP (lander) – plasma density; SHAPE (Propulsion Module) – observes Earth from lunar orbit.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-3 payloads:
1. The APXS found the lunar soil to be rich in aluminium.
2. The Laser Retroreflector Array (LRA) on the lander is a passive instrument of NASA.
3. The LIBS on the rover confirmed sulphur on the lunar surface in situ.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: APXS found the soil rich in iron and magnesium and poor in aluminium.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan):
1. It entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014.
2. It made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit.
3. With it ISRO became the fourth agency to reach Mars, after NASA, Roscosmos and CNSA.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the three earlier agencies were NASA, USSR/Roscosmos and ESA, not China's CNSA.

s:
Consider the following statements about Mangalyaan:
1. It carried seven scientific payloads.
2. The Methane Sensor for Mars was one of its payloads.
3. Designed for six months, it worked for about eight years until contact was lost in 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: MOM carried 5 payloads (Methane Sensor for Mars, Lyman Alpha Photometer, Mars Colour Camera, MENCA, TIS).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Methane in the Martian atmosphere is cited, with water and gypsum, as evidence for possible life on Mars.
Reason (R): Methane on Mars was first measured by NASA's Spirit rover.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: methane on Mars was first measured by ESA's Mars Express (also by NASA's Curiosity), not by Spirit.

s:
Match List-I (Space shuttle) with List-II (Fact):
List-I (Shuttle) | List-II (Fact)
a. Columbia | i. Last shuttle mission, STS-135 (2011)
b. Challenger | ii. First shuttle flight, STS-1 (1981)
c. Discovery | iii. Hubble servicing with six new gyroscopes (Dec 1999)
d. Atlantis | iv. Crew repaired the Solar Maximum Mission (1984)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Columbia flew STS-1 (Apr 1981); Challenger's crew repaired the Solar Maximum Mission (STS-41C, 1984); Discovery serviced Hubble in Dec 1999 (STS-103); Atlantis flew the last mission STS-135 (Jul 2011).

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-2:
1. Its Vikram lander crash-landed at Jawahar Point in September 2019.
2. The Union Cabinet approved the mission in 2008.
3. Its orbiter is still working.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: Vikram hard-landed at Tiranga Point; Jawahar Point is the impact site of Chandrayaan-1's Moon Impact Probe.

s:
Consider the following statements about Aditya-L1:
1. It was launched by PSLV-C57 from the Second Launch Pad at Sriharikota.
2. It orbits the Sun-Earth L1 point, about 15 million km from the Earth.
3. It was inserted into its halo orbit on 6 January 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: L1 is about 1.5 million km from the Earth.

s:
Match List-I (Aditya-L1 payload) with List-II (What it studies):
List-I (Payload) | List-II (Studies)
a. VELC | i. Hard X-rays
b. SUIT | ii. Photosphere and chromosphere (near-UV)
c. HEL1OS | iii. Solar corona
d. PAPA | iv. Solar-wind electrons and ions
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: VELC – corona; SUIT – photosphere and chromosphere in near-UV; HEL1OS – hard X-ray (SoLEXS is soft X-ray); PAPA – solar-wind electrons and ions.

s:
Consider the following statements about Aditya-L1 payloads:
1. The VELC was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
2. The SUIT was built by IUCAA.
3. Aditya-L1 carries seven payloads – four remote-sensing and three in-situ.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: VELC (IIA), SUIT (IUCAA); 7 payloads = 4 remote sensing (VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS) + 3 in-situ (ASPEX, PAPA, magnetometer).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. AstroSat observes in the X-ray, optical and UV bands simultaneously.
2. UVIT and LAXPC are payloads of AstroSat.
3. The POLIX payload of XPoSat was developed by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: POLIX was developed by the Raman Research Institute, Bengaluru.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-1:
1. It carried 11 scientific instruments, including NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper.
2. The Lyman Alpha Photometer was one of its instruments.
3. NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper on it detected water molecules on the lunar surface.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Lyman Alpha Photometer flew on Mangalyaan; Chandrayaan-1 carried Mini-SAR, CIXS, TMC, M3 etc.

s:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-1:
1. Its Moon Impact Probe hit the south polar region on 14 November 2008.
2. The impact site is named Shiv Shakti Point.
3. Contact with the spacecraft was lost on 29 August 2009.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the MIP site is Jawahar Point; Shiv Shakti Point is Chandrayaan-3's landing site.

s:
Match List-I (Mission) with List-II (Launch vehicle):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Vehicle)
a. AstroSat | i. LVM3-M4
b. Chandrayaan-2 | ii. PSLV-C30
c. Chandrayaan-3 | iii. GSLV Mk III-M1
d. SpaDeX | iv. PSLV-C60
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: AstroSat – PSLV-C30 (2015); Chandrayaan-2 – GSLV Mk III-M1 (2019); Chandrayaan-3 – LVM3-M4 (2023); SpaDeX – PSLV-C60 (30 Dec 2024), which made India the 4th country to dock.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A two-body system has five Lagrange points where a small object can stay balanced.
2. A Hohmann transfer is a fuel-saving elliptical transfer between two orbits using two burns.
3. The Mars Orbiter Mission used a Hohmann transfer to reach Mars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Lagrange points L1–L5; a Hohmann transfer is an elliptical two-burn transfer, used by MOM after Earth orbit-raising.

s:
Match List-I (Mission) with List-II (Aim):
List-I (Mission) | List-II (Aim)
a. Shukrayaan-1 | i. Mars landing
b. Chandrayaan-4 | ii. Lunar sample return
c. Mangalyaan-2 | iii. Earth – hazards and climate
d. NISAR | iv. Venus orbiter
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Shukrayaan-1 – Venus orbiter; Chandrayaan-4 – lunar sample return from the south polar region (2028); Mangalyaan-2 – Mars landing (~2030); NISAR – NASA-ISRO Earth observation.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Union Cabinet approved the Venus Orbiter Mission in September 2024 at a cost of Rs 1,236 crore.
2. Under Space Vision 2047, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is to be set up by 2035.
3. Under Space Vision 2047, an Indian is to land on the Moon by 2047.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the target for an Indian on the Moon is 2040.

s:
Consider the following statements about human spaceflight:
1. Alan Shepard was the first American in space, while John Glenn was the first American to orbit the Earth.
2. China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei, flew on Shenzhou-5 in October 2003.
3. So far only the USSR/Russia, the USA and Japan have launched humans into space on their own.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the three nations with their own crewed launch are USSR/Russia, USA and China; India (Gaganyaan) would be the fourth.

s:
Match List-I (Astronaut) with List-II (Distinction):
List-I (Astronaut) | List-II (Distinction)
a. Rakesh Sharma | i. Indian-origin NASA astronaut on Soyuz MS-29 (2026)
b. Kalpana Chawla | ii. First Indian in space (Soyuz T-11, 1984)
c. Shubhanshu Shukla | iii. First Indian on the ISS
d. Anil Menon | iv. First Indian-origin woman in space (1997)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Rakesh Sharma – Soyuz T-11, Apr 1984; Kalpana Chawla – first Indian-origin woman in space (NASA, 1997); Shubhanshu Shukla – first Indian on the ISS (Axiom-4); Anil Menon – Soyuz MS-29, Jul 2026, eight months.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Axiom-4 mission:
1. It was launched on 25 June 2025 in a SpaceX Dragon on a Falcon 9 rocket.
2. Shubhanshu Shukla stayed about 28 days aboard the ISS.
3. Its crew, commanded by Peggy Whitson, included astronauts from Poland and Hungary.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the crew spent 18 days on the ISS (returned 15 Jul 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements about Gaganyaan:
1. It was approved in 2018 as India's first human spaceflight programme.
2. It aims to take a crew of three to a low Earth orbit of about 400 km for seven days.
3. The crew module is to splash down in Indian waters and be recovered by the Indian Navy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the planned mission lasts 3 days (crew of 3, ~400 km LEO).

s:
Consider the following statements about Gaganyaan:
1. It will be launched by the human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3) from Sriharikota.
2. The CE-20 engine for the L110 stage of the human-rated LVM3 was qualified in three tests.
3. DRDO provides human-centric systems such as parachutes, life support and crew recovery.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the engine of the L110 stage is the Vikas engine, qualified in 3 tests (CE-20 is the cryogenic engine).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Gaganyaan's Orbital Module has only two parts – the Crew Module and the Service Module.
Reason (R): Russia's Soyuz and China's Shenzhou spacecraft each have three modules – orbital, descent and service.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true, but R only contrasts other spacecraft; it does not explain why Gaganyaan has two parts.

s:
Match List-I (Gaganyaan test) with List-II (What it tested):
List-I (Test) | List-II (What it tested)
a. CARE (2014) | i. Crew Escape System abort at Mach 1.2
b. TV-D1 (2023) | ii. 5.7 t module with 10 parachutes of 4 types
c. IADT-01 (2025) | iii. Crew-module re-entry
d. IADT-02 (2026) | iv. 4.8 t module dropped from a Chinook helicopter
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: CARE (LVM3-X, 18 Dec 2014) – re-entry; TV-D1 (18 Oct 2023) – crew escape at Mach 1.2; IADT-01 (24 Aug 2025) – 4.8 t from 3 km by IAF Chinook; IADT-02 (10 Apr 2026) – 5.7 t, 10 parachutes.

s:
Consider the following statements about Gaganyaan tests:
1. The TV-D1 test flight was conducted at Sriharikota.
2. IADT-01, the first Integrated Air Drop Test, was conducted at SDSC-SHAR.
3. SOLVE (July 2026) was an air-drop test of the crew module parachutes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: SOLVE (3 Jul 2026) was a solid-motor ground test.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Gaganyatris named in February 2024:
1. All four are Indian Air Force test pilots.
2. Their selection and aeromedical tests were carried out by the IAF's Institute of Aerospace Medicine, Bengaluru.
3. Their zero-gravity training is given in a centrifuge.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: zero-g training is given through aircraft parabolic flights.

s:
Consider the following statements about the International Space Station:
1. It has been continuously crewed since November 2000.
2. It is expected to retire around 2035.
3. Its module Kibo was contributed by Japan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the ISS is expected to retire around 2030.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS):
1. The full station is to be completed by 2040.
2. It was approved in September 2024 and will have five modules.
3. Its base module BAS-1 is targeted for 2028 on the LVM3.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the full BAS is targeted for 2035; 2040 is the target for an Indian on the Moon.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): The mass of an astronaut in an orbiting satellite becomes zero.
Reason (R): In an orbiting satellite the craft and the astronaut fall with the same acceleration, so the normal force on the astronaut is zero.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is false: in weightlessness the weight (felt as normal force) becomes zero but the mass stays the same. R is true: free fall with the same g makes the normal force zero.

s:
Match List-I (Condition in microgravity) with List-II (Effect):
List-I (Condition) | List-II (Effect)
a. Bone loss | i. Space motion sickness
b. Fluid shift | ii. Weakening of postural muscles
c. Space Adaptation Syndrome | iii. 1–1.5% of bone mass a month
d. Muscle atrophy | iv. 'Puffy face, bird legs'
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Bone loss – 1–1.5% a month; fluid shift – puffy face, bird legs (Charlie Brown effect); Space Adaptation Syndrome – space motion sickness; muscle atrophy – postural muscles weaken.

s:
Match List-I (Facility) with List-II (Role / feature):
List-I (Facility) | List-II (Role)
a. Human Space Flight Centre, Bengaluru | i. Tracking network
b. ISTRAC, Bengaluru | ii. New ISRO vertical leading Gaganyaan
c. Dhanush, Sriharikota | iii. SSLV launch complex
d. Kulasekarapattinam, Tamil Nadu | iv. India's first private launch pad (Agnikul Cosmos)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: HSFC – new ISRO vertical for Gaganyaan; ISTRAC – tracking network; Dhanush – Agnikul Cosmos' private pad; Kulasekarapattinam – SSLV complex (foundation 27 Aug 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements about the Third Launch Pad at Sriharikota:
1. The Union Cabinet approved it in January 2025.
2. It will cost about Rs 10,000 crore.
3. It is meant for the Next Generation Launch Vehicle (NGLV) and human spaceflight.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the approved cost is about Rs 4,000 crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about analogue missions in Ladakh:
1. India's first analogue space mission at Leh (November 2024) was conducted by ISRO with AAKA and IIT Madras.
2. The HOPE habitat at Tso Kar was chosen because its conditions resemble early Mars – high UV, low pressure and cold.
3. MITRA was a crew behavioural study at Leh with the IAF's Institute of Aerospace Medicine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: the partner institute was IIT Bombay.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RISAT series:
1. RISAT-2 (2009), launched on PSLV-C12 with ANUSAT, carried an Israeli-built X-band radar.
2. RISAT-1 (2012), with a C-band SAR, was India's first fully indigenous radar imaging satellite.
3. In 2019 RISAT-2B performed a collision-avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using GAGAN data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the manoeuvre used data from NETRA, ISRO's space-situational-awareness project; GAGAN is a navigation augmentation system.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): EOS-09 (RISAT-1B), a C-band SAR satellite, was lost on the PSLV-C61 mission in 2025.
Reason (R): PSLV-C61 failed because of a roll-rate disturbance at the end of its third stage.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: A is true. R is false: PSLV-C61 failed after a pressure drop in the third-stage solid motor; the roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage caused the PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 failure (Jan 2026).

Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (Built by):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (Builder)
a. SRMSAT | i. SRM University, Chennai
b. SATYABAMASAT | ii. Sathyabama University, Chennai
c. Jugnu | iii. IIT Kanpur
d. Kalamsat-V2 | iv. Space Kidz India
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: SRMSAT – SRM University (PSLV-C18, 2011); SATYABAMASAT – Sathyabama University (PSLV-C34, 2016); Jugnu – IIT Kanpur (PSLV-C18, 2011); Kalamsat-V2 – Space Kidz India (PSLV-C44, 2019).

s:
Consider the following statements about student satellites:
1. ANUSAT (2009) of Anna University was the first satellite built by an Indian university.
2. StudSat, India's first pico-satellite, was built by IIT Bombay.
3. AzaadiSAT, built by 750 girl students with Space Kidz India, was launched on SSLV-D1 but failed to reach orbit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: StudSat (PSLV-C15, 2010) was built by seven engineering colleges of Karnataka and undivided Andhra Pradesh.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. WESAT, the first satellite fully built by women students, was made by the LBS Institute of Technology for Women, Thiruvananthapuram.
2. WESAT measures groundwater recharge by rainfall.
3. GSAT-1, the first payload of the GSLV (2001), is not a student satellite.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: WESAT (POEM-3, PSLV-C58) measures solar ultraviolet radiation, not groundwater.

Match List-I (ISRO programme) with List-II (Meant for / run with):
List-I (Programme) | List-II (Feature)
a. UNNATI | i. 75 Eklavya Model Residential Schools
b. YUVIKA | ii. Indian school students of Class 9
c. ATL Space Challenge | iii. Nanosatellite training for engineers of developing countries
d. Space Labs | iv. Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: UNNATI (2019, 50 years of UNISPACE-I) – developing-country engineers; YUVIKA (Yuva Vigyani Karyakram) – Class 9 students; ATL Space Challenge – AIM + ISRO + CBSE; Space Labs – 75 EMRS (Apr 2026).

s:
Consider the following statements about PSLV-C37 (15 February 2017):
1. Its main satellite was a Cartosat-2 series satellite.
2. Its 101 foreign nanosatellites came from six countries.
3. Its 104 satellites in one launch is still the world record.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the world record is now SpaceX Transporter-1 (143 satellites, Jan 2021); 104 is still ISRO's record.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. By 1 January 2026, Indian rockets had launched over 400 foreign satellites.
2. PSLV-C62 (January 2026) carried 15 co-passengers from start-ups and academic institutions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: over 400 foreign satellites by 1 Jan 2026; PSLV-C62 carried 15 start-up and academic co-passengers.

Match List-I (Satellite) with List-II (User):
List-I (Satellite) | List-II (User)
a. GSAT-7 'Rukmini' | i. Indian Army
b. GSAT-7A 'Angry Bird' | ii. DRDO
c. GSAT-7B | iii. Indian Navy
d. EMISAT | iv. Indian Air Force
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: GSAT-7 (2013) – Navy; GSAT-7A (2018) – Air Force, network-centric warfare; GSAT-7B – Army (planned); EMISAT (2019) – DRDO, electronic intelligence.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. GSAT-7 was launched by Ariane-5 in 2013.
2. GSAT-7R (CMS-03), launched on LVM3-M5 on 2 November 2025, serves the Indian Air Force.
3. GSAT-7R is the heaviest Indian communication satellite.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: GSAT-7R serves the Indian Navy, replacing GSAT-7.

s:
Consider the following statements about defence space:
1. The SBS-3 programme, approved in November 2024, envisages 52 satellites, 31 of them built by private industry.
2. The tri-service Defence Space Agency was set up in 2019 at New Delhi.
3. The Defence Space Research Organisation (DSRO) is the R&D arm of the Defence Space Agency.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the Defence Space Agency (2019) is at Bengaluru.

s:
Consider the following statements about Vikram-S:
1. It was launched under Mission Prarambh on 18 November 2022.
2. Its developer, Skyroot Aerospace, is based in Bengaluru.
3. It reached an altitude of 89.5 km on its suborbital flight.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: Skyroot Aerospace is based in Hyderabad.

s:
Consider the following statements about Skyroot's Vikram-1:
1. It is a four-stage rocket that can carry 350 kg to low Earth orbit.
2. It was launched under Mission Aagaman on 18 July 2026.
3. With it India became the third country, after the United States and Russia, to have private orbital launch capability.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: the two earlier countries were the United States and China.

Match List-I (Company) with List-II (Product):
List-I (Company) | List-II (Product)
a. Agnikul Cosmos | i. Dhanush private launch pad
b. Bellatrix Aerospace | ii. Green propulsion and electric thrusters
c. GalaxEye | iii. Drishti SAR + optical satellite
d. Pixxel | iv. Firefly hyperspectral constellation
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: Agnikul Cosmos – Agnibaan, Agnilet and the Dhanush pad at Sriharikota; Bellatrix – 1N green propulsion, electric thrusters; GalaxEye – Drishti (SAR + optical); Pixxel – Firefly, first Indian private commercial constellation (Jan 2025).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The POEM platform built on the PSLV's fourth stage was conceived and realised by URSC, Bengaluru.
2. Agnikul Cosmos, incubated at IIT Madras, is based in Chennai.
3. Bellatrix Aerospace's green propulsion system, demonstrated on PSLV-C58's POEM-3, was developed under DRDO's Technology Development Fund.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 2 and 3 are correct. 1 is wrong: POEM (PSLV Orbital Experimental Module) was realised by VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram.

s:
Consider the following statements about Indian private space firms:
1. Pixxel leads the public-private Earth-observation constellation approved by IN-SPACe.
2. Dhruva Space, maker of nanosatellite platforms, is based in Hyderabad.
3. Digantara builds hyperspectral imaging satellites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Digantara (Bengaluru) works on space situational awareness; hyperspectral imaging is Pixxel's field.

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A): Agnikul Cosmos's private launch pad Dhanush and its mission control are located at Sriharikota.
Reason (R): Sriharikota in Andhra Pradesh is India's only operational spaceport.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: as Sriharikota is India's only operational spaceport, Agnikul set up its pad Dhanush and mission control there.

s:
Consider the following statements about NSIL missions:
1. Under its demand-driven model, NSIL builds, owns and operates satellites against assured customer demand.
2. GSAT-24 was launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou, French Guiana.
3. GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20) was launched by the LVM3 in November 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: GSAT-N2 flew on SpaceX's Falcon 9 (19 Nov 2024) because Indian rockets lacked the capacity.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Space Policy 2023:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 6 April 2023 and released by the Department of Space on 20 April 2023.
2. It seeks to privatise ISRO and reduce it to a regulatory body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only 1 is correct. 2 is wrong: ISRO moves out of operational and commercial production to focus on R&D, but it 'will not be privatised or reduced' to a regulatory body.

s:
Match List-I (Entity) with List-II (Role under the Indian Space Policy 2023):
List-I (Entity) | List-II (Role)
a. ISRO | i. Advanced R&D, deep space missions and human spaceflight
b. IN-SPACe | ii. Promotes, authorises and supervises non-governmental entities
c. NSIL | iii. Commercialises mature ISRO technologies
d. Department of Space | iv. Policy, space diplomacy and treaty compliance
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
x: ISRO – advanced R&D, deep space, human spaceflight; IN-SPACe – independent regulator of NGEs; NSIL – commercialises mature ISRO technology; DoS – policy, space diplomacy, treaty compliance.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Antrix Corporation, set up in September 1992, got Miniratna status in 2008 and followed a supply-driven model.
2. NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), set up in 2019, is a CPSE under the Ministry of Electronics and IT.
3. NSIL is headquartered at Bengaluru.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: NSIL is a CPSE under the Department of Space, the commercial arm of ISRO.

s:
Consider the following statements about IN-SPACe:
1. It was set up in 2020 as an autonomous single-window agency under the Department of Space, with headquarters at Ahmedabad.
2. It is chaired by Dr S. Somanath.
3. It enabled the transfer of SSLV technology to private consortia.
How many of the above statements are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: the chairman of IN-SPACe is Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka.

Consider the following statements about automatic-route FDI limits in the space sector:
1. Satellite components and subsystems – up to 100%.
2. Launch vehicles and spaceports – up to 74%.
3. Satellite manufacturing, operation and data products – up to 74%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 3 are correct. 2 is wrong: launch vehicles and spaceports are allowed up to 49% on the automatic route.

Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's space plans:
1. AP Space Policy 4.0 targets an investment of Rs 25,000 crore during 2025-35.
2. The Tirupati Space City is planned over about 3,000 acres near Sriharikota.
3. The Lepakshi Space City is meant to host a second spaceport.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: 1 and 2 are correct. 3 is wrong: Lepakshi Space City is meant for research and development.
